findings.reason: The facts hold: diff.patch deletes the guarded block in src/common/utils.ts normalizeReference, and package.json has no engines field. But the deleted comment itself says to remove the block once Node v10 is no longer supported. Node 10 went end-of-life in 2021, and this package already depends on modern-Node features (an exports map, ESM bin, node --test). So dropping the dead workaround is what this change is meant to do, not a defect in it.
findings.claim: Removing the Node v10 'ẞ' case-folding workaround without a declared engines minimum may silently break reference-label matching for Node 10 users.
findings.evidence: The diff deletes the runtime-guarded block in normalizeReference (src/common/utils.ts) `if ('ẞ'.toLowerCase() === 'Ṿ') { str = str.replace(/ẞ/g, 'ß') }`, whose comment said 'remove this when node v10 is no longer supported'. A search of package.json finds no `engines` field. CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml:23) only tests `node-version: lts/*`, so no run would show the regression on old runtimes. The fixtures test/fixtures/commonmark/good.txt and spec.txt contain 'ẞ', so the behaviour is still covered on modern Node.
